issues.description: validate_conda filter '*.exe' will block selecting conda/mamba executables on macOS and Linux
issues.detail: In confpage.py the file browser is created with filters='*.exe'. On Linux and macOS, conda/mamba/micromamba binaries have no extension (e.g. /opt/homebrew/bin/conda, ~/miniconda3/bin/conda). The platform-agnostic filter will hide all valid executables on non-Windows systems, making the feature unusable on the majority of Spyder's user base. The filter should be platform-conditional or use a generic 'All files (*)' fallback alongside '*.exe' on Windows.

issues.description: validate_conda's os.access(X_OK) check will always fail on Windows for .exe paths in some setups and is fragile across platforms
issues.detail: os.access(path, os.X_OK) has well-known unreliability on Windows (it inspects the extension rather than ACLs) and can also reject scripts/symlinks on Unix where the user can still invoke them via shells. Since the validator already executes the binary with --version, the X_OK gate is redundant and risks rejecting legitimate executables. Removing the os.X_OK check (or relying solely on the --version probe) is more robust.

issues.description: validate_conda substring match is too permissive — any path containing 'mamba'/'conda' in its --version stdout passes
issues.detail: The check `any(tool in out.decode().lower() for tool in ['micromamba', 'mamba', 'conda'])` will accept any program whose --version output happens to contain those substrings (e.g. a wrapper script, an unrelated tool named 'condabridge', or even a localized error message). A stricter check should anchor on the start of the output (e.g. startswith) or parse for the expected 'conda X.Y.Z' format. Note also that 'micromamba' is redundant — 'mamba' already matches it.

issues.description: validate_conda does not decode stderr and may miss output from tools that print --version to stderr
issues.detail: Some versions of conda/mamba historically print version info to stderr rather than stdout. Only the first element of communicate() (stdout) is inspected; stderr is discarded via `__`. If run_program's Popen wasn't configured to merge streams, a legitimate executable could be flagged invalid. Either merge stderr into stdout or check both streams.

issues.description: kernelspec.argv() uses custom conda_path even when it is invalid or empty whitespace
issues.detail: In kernelspec.py the code reads `self.get_conf('conda_path', ...)` and uses it directly if `custom_conda` is truthy. There is no re-validation at runtime — a user could toggle the checkbox after entering an invalid path that bypassed validation (e.g. by editing settings file directly, or by entering a path then deleting the binary). The code should validate again or fall back gracefully with a clearer error pointing to the preferences page.

issues.description: conda_edit attribute is set but no validation/state coupling between checkbox and stored path
issues.detail: self.conda_edit is assigned but there is no apply/save logic shown that clears conda_path when custom_conda is unchecked, nor is there a requirement that conda_path be set when custom_conda is checked. A user could enable the checkbox with an empty path, which validate_conda explicitly returns True for (empty string short-circuit), then hit the SpyderKernelError at runtime since `if not conda_exe` will fall through. The empty-string-is-valid behavior also means saving with the checkbox on and an empty path produces silent failure later.

issues.description: setFocus() side effect added to select_file is unscoped and may surprise other callers
issues.detail: The change in widgets/config.py adds `edit.setFocus()` unconditionally after select_file populates the line edit. This generic widget helper is used by many config pages, so all browse-file controls across Spyder will now grab focus after selection. The intent is presumably to trigger the validation callback on focus-out — but that contract is implicit and untested for other callers. A targeted approach (e.g. an explicit validate() call, or a parameter) is safer.

issues.description: Tooltip text says 'Conda/Mamba' but mentions only 'Conda/Mamba installed at non-standard location', omitting micromamba
issues.detail: The checkbox label and tooltip variously mention 'Conda/Mamba/Micromamba' and 'Conda/Mamba' inconsistently. Minor copy issue but worth normalizing for clarity.

issues.description: HTML markup in user-facing error message may not render in all SpyderKernelError contexts
issues.detail:
The new error message uses `

` and `` tags. If the error is surfaced in a plain-text dialog or logged to a console, the user will see literal tags. Worth confirming the consuming widget renders rich text.

issues.description: No tests added for validate_conda or the new config-flow behavior
issues.detail: validate_conda is a pure-ish helper that's straightforward to unit-test (empty string, nonexistent file, non-executable, wrong --version output, valid). The PR adds no test coverage, and the kernel selection branching in kernelspec.argv() also has no regression test. Given the user-facing impact and cross-platform concerns, at least minimal unit tests would substantially de-risk this change.

issues.description: 'last_envs': {} loses trailing comma in original; new key added without preserving formatting consistency
issues.detail: Minor: the dict literal in config/main.py now ends with `'conda_path': '',` while the previous trailing item didn't have a comma. Not a bug, just style — but worth noting for code-style consistency in the Spyder repo.

dissents.topic: Whether empty conda_path with custom_conda=True should be considered valid

positions.position: validate_conda returning True for empty string is correct — it lets users clear the field without an error dialog. The 'is the user actually using it' check belongs at runtime.
If custom_conda is enabled, an empty conda_path is a logically invalid state; validation should fail and surface the issue at config time, not as a cryptic kernel error later.

dissents.topic: Scope of widgets/config.py select_file change (adding setFocus)

positions.position: Tiny one-line change; focus moving to the edited field after selection is generally a fine UX improvement and unlikely to break anyone.
Modifying a widely-used shared helper to support a single new caller's validation flow is a leaky cross-cutting change. The new behavior should be opt-in or implemented inside the conda confpage.
Substring match across three names is too loose; should anchor on startswith and parse a semver-shaped token. Otherwise a maliciously named binary or wrapper could pass.

This validator is a soft hint for the user, not a security boundary. False positives are unlikely in practice; substring match is good enough and avoids over-fitting to specific version-string formats that vary between conda forks.

review.summary: The PR adds a useful, well-scoped feature (custom Conda executable preference) to address #20357, and the kernelspec fallback chain is sensible. However, the file-picker filter `*.exe` is a P0 cross-platform blocker that makes the feature effectively unusable on macOS/Linux — Conda binaries there have no extension. Secondary concerns cluster around validate_conda's robustness (over-permissive substring match, fragile os.access check, ignored stderr) and the absence of runtime re-validation or empty-path handling when the checkbox is enabled. A small but unscoped change to the shared select_file helper (unconditional setFocus) deserves a more targeted implementation. No tests accompany the change despite easy testability of the helper.
